Good morning, Shahriaar. Today is Wednesday, November 25. This is your morning brief.

Weather today is 9 degrees Celsius, clear skies. The high will be 19 and the low 9 degrees Celsius. Chance of precipitation is 0 percent.

You have 8 appointments in the next 24 hours: 10:00 AM, Meeting with Mr. Fallah; 10:00 AM, innovation Hub; 11:00 AM, PR-cheese -(development region); 11:30 AM, PR-cheese -(west region); 12:00 PM, PR-cheese -(north-east region); 12:30 PM, PR-cheese -(north-west region); 1:00 PM, PR-cheese -(central region); 1:30 PM, PR-cheese -(south region).

Now, the top 5 stories in AI today.

First, from TechCrunch: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to U.S. industrial might — not a champion. Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is celebrating a company that has helped put advanced chips in its adversaries' hands.

Second, from WIRED: Jensen Huang’s Return Shows Nvidia Is Too Big to Police. Nvidia’s place at the center of the US economy may have outweighed concerns about its CEO’s ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, national security and foreign policy experts say.

Third, from TechCrunch: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy. It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.

Fourth, from TechCrunch: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy. The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.

Fifth, from TechCrunch: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life. As millions embrace personal AI assistants, a new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without introducing potential new problems.

That is your brief. Have a great day.
